text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The fact that the government has ordered the Employees' Provident Fund to participate in the development of low-cost houses should not be an excuse for developers to shrug off their social responsibility in meeting the housing needs of the lower-income group, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said today.
- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad turned the heat on the West at the World Solar Summit, saying that their lukewarm response shows an attempt to block the rays of hope to developing countries.
- The problem of legal foreign workers bringing in contagious diseases has worsened because stringent screening measures are not enforced, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
- Razali Ismail, who officially assumed the presidency of the 51st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York yesterday, plans to resolve problems plaguing the world body.
- Malaysia's exports to South countries have increased significantly over the last five years to reach 32.1 billion ringgit in 1995, International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz says.

- Metroplex Bhd has on Monday entered into a memorandum of agreement with Philippine conglomerate, Belle Group, to construct and develop a Las Vegas-style 15,000 sq metre casino and hotel Belle Bay Plaza complex in Manila.
